question: In what kinds of ML methods is feature scaling especially important, and why?
direct_answer: It is especially important in distance-based, gradient-based, and variance-based methods because those methods depend on numeric scale.
expanded_answer: Feature scaling matters most when the algorithm uses geometry or optimization directly. For k-NN, k-means, and many clustering methods, scale affects distances and assignments. For linear models trained with gradient descent, scaling can improve conditioning and speed convergence. For PCA and other covariance-based methods, scale changes which directions appear most variable. Tree-based models are often less sensitive because they split on thresholds rather than Euclidean distances, though scaling can still matter in some pipelines.
common_wrong_ideas: Scaling is only for neural networks
Tree models always need scaling just like k-NN
If one model does not need scaling, no model does
